headline: High: shared file-based content flow can drive prompt injection and cascading posting errors; data leakage is limited by B's no-read/no-write profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa can ingest text/voice and connect to messaging APIs, while social-auto-upload operates on local media/account files and CLI workflows. No direct shared channel is documented, but if A’s outputs are copied into B’s upload inputs or captions, B could treat attacker-controlled text as trusted instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not proven.
conditions: IF operator copies Rasa-generated text into social-auto-upload captions or metadata
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridges A outputs into B inputs
mitigations: Use a manual review step before any caption or description is pasted into uploads.
Strip instructions, URLs, and markup from A-generated text before reuse.
Keep A and B in separate workspaces with no shared clipboard sync.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to content passed from A to B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and has allowlisted egress; social-auto-upload touches video, images, and account data but its profile shows no filesystem read/write and no shell. Without a shared workspace or explicit file handoff, leakage from A into B is not established. If operators manually move sensitive text into B’s files, the blast radius is limited to uploaded media/account context.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or manual file transfer is introduced between A and B
IF sensitive text from A is embedded into B upload assets or account metadata
mitigations: Keep customer-support transcripts out of upload folders.
Store A and B artifacts in separate directories.
Review B input files for accidental inclusion of chat logs.
Rotate any exposed account credentials immediately if copied into files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is documented as not supporting multiple instances, while social-auto-upload supports multiple instances but has no filesystem write, git, or shell capability. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable directory
IF additional undocumented write or git capabilities are enabled
mitigations: Keep each agent in its own directory.
Do not grant shared write access to account files.
Avoid running both against the same git checkout.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles if a shared mutable store is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can generate conversational text, and social-auto-upload can act on local files and account data to publish content. If A’s output is reused as B’s upload text or metadata without verification, B may propagate hallucinated or unsafe content to public platforms. The interaction is inferred from documented I/O surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF A-generated text is inserted into B captions, descriptions, or filenames
IF B publishes content without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human approval before each upload.
Compare A-generated claims against source material before posting.
Use a template that separates facts from free-form text.
Log the exact A output used by B for later review.

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa handles text and voice, while social-auto-upload handles video, images, and account data. The profiles do not show PHI, residency, or retention mismatches, so only a generic compliance gap is visible: if support transcripts are repurposed into social uploads, policy violations could occur. The other agent is not cited separately because no residency or certification data is present.
conditions: IF regulated support transcripts are copied into social-auto-upload assets
IF retention or deletion policies differ for the same customer data class
mitigations: Do not reuse support transcripts in public uploads.
Check whether any uploaded media contains personal data.
Delete accidental customer data from upload folders within five minutes.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across systems.
